sections.eyebrow: Pottery studio on Quay Lane, Wrenmouth
sections.heading: Learn to throw pots in an old sail loft *by the quay.*
sections.lede: Saltmarsh is a teaching pottery and shared studio. Come for a two-hour taster, an eight-week course, or a shelf and a wheel of your own.
sections.caption: Finished work on the collection shelves.

sections.heading: Four ways to get your hands in the clay
sections.intro: Classes are capped at eight people, so there is always a wheel each and a tutor nearby.

items.title: Taster session
items.text: Two hours on the wheel with a tutor. You keep your best two pots, which we glaze and fire for you.

items.title: Eight-week wheel course
items.text: One evening a week. Centring, pulling walls, trimming and glazing, in that order and at your own pace.

items.title: Hand-building evenings
items.text: Pinch, coil and slab work around the long table. Drop in when you like; no booking past the first visit.

items.title: Studio membership
items.text: Your own shelf, a key, and the wheels whenever a class is not running. Glazes and firing are included.

sections.heading: A working pottery, not a showroom
body: Nell Harcourt opened Saltmarsh in 2011 with two second-hand wheels and a kiln bought from a school that was closing its art block.

It is still a place where things get made. There is slip on the floor, test tiles on every sill, and usually a kettle on. Members work alongside classes, which is how most people here learned the things no course covers.

points.title: Stoneware, fired to 1240°C
points.text: Everything made here is safe for food, ovens and dishwashers.

points.title: Glazes mixed in house
points.text: Sixteen on the board at the moment, all lead-free.

sections.heading: What people have been making
sections.intro: Student and member work from recent firings. Most of it has gone home by now.

items.quote: I came for a taster and stayed three years. Nobody rushes you, and nobody pretends your first bowl is any good.
items.name: Priya N.

items.quote: The eight weeks went quickly. By week five I had made a mug I now use every morning.
items.name: Tom A.

items.quote: We booked the taster for a birthday. All six of us got a wheel, and our pots were ready in a fortnight.
items.name: Hannah R.

sections.heading: Questions we get asked a lot

items.a: No. The taster and the eight-week course both start from nothing. If you have thrown before, tell the tutor and they will set you something harder.
Clothes you do not mind getting clay on, and short nails if you can manage it. Aprons and towels are here.

items.q: When do I get my pots?
items.a: About two weeks after you make them. They have to dry, be fired once, glazed, and fired again. We email when they are on the collection shelf.
Tasters are for ages twelve and up, with an adult. Saturday morning family sessions take ages six and up.

items.q: Do you fire work made elsewhere?
items.a: Yes, if it is stoneware clay from a supplier we know. Bring the bag label with you the first time.

sections.heading: Up the stairs behind the chandlery
sections.intro: Call in whenever we are open. Someone will show you round, and there is no need to book for a look.

sections.heading: New wheel courses start every January, April and September.
sections.text: Places go to the waiting list first, so it is worth adding your name.

pages.title: The studio
pages.description: Saltmarsh Pottery has been teaching in the Sail Loft on Quay Lane since 2011. Twelve wheels, three kilns and sixteen house glazes.
pages.intro: Twelve wheels, three kilns and a long table, in a loft where sails were once cut and stitched.

sections.heading: How it started
body: Nell Harcourt trained as a production thrower in Stoke-on-Trent and moved to Wrenmouth in 2009. She opened Saltmarsh two years later with two second-hand wheels and a kiln from a school that was closing its art block.
The loft had been empty since the sailmakers left. It has north light, a hoist that still works and a floor that slopes just enough to notice.

pages.title: Privacy
pages.description: How Saltmarsh Pottery uses the details you give us when you book.

blocks.text: We keep as little about you as we can. This page says what we hold and why.

items: Your name, email address and phone number, so we can confirm a booking.
The classes you have booked and paid for.
Anything you tell us that affects your class, such as access needs.

blocks.text: We do not sell or share your details, and this website sets no tracking cookies. We email you about a booking, and about new course dates only if you asked to join the waiting list.
Email the studio and we will send you everything we hold, correct it or delete it, whichever you ask for.
